cards.title: AI can misread. AICA plans for it.
cards.body: Doctor handwriting challenges everyone, including software. In healthcare a wrong word matters, so AICA is designed around checking, not blind trust.

cards.title: AI reads, it doesn't decide
cards.body: AI pulls medicine names, doses and timings from the photo. That's a draft, not a record.

cards.title: Photo and reading, side by side
cards.body: You compare what AI read against the original prescription photo, line by line, and fix anything that looks wrong.

cards.title: Nothing saved until you confirm
cards.body: Reminders and records are created only after a person confirms. No silent saves straight from the AI.

cards.title: The doctor's word stays the doctor's
cards.body: AICA follows what the prescription says. Any question about a dose or a change goes to your doctor or pharmacist.

cards.title: Help for the counter too
cards.body: Pharmacies get AI help reading handwriting as well, working alongside the pharmacist who knows the job.

cards.title: Honest AI means people in charge
cards.body: AI to speed things up, people to make sure it's right. See how it works in the prototype at aicaglobal.in.

takeaway: AICA's AI drafts the reading, a person checks it against the photo, and nothing is saved without confirmation.
share: AICA's rule for AI: it reads the prescription, you confirm it. Nothing saved without a human check.
